title: 3 Myths Keeping You From Great Classroom Management https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2021/02/12/3-myths-from-great-classroom-management/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Anticipating a return to in-person teaching after a period when online instruction had largely eliminated misbehavior, Linsin warns that classroom management struggles from before the pandemic will simply resume unless directly addressed. He identifies three myths keeping teachers stuck: that some people simply can't manage a classroom well, that skill improves automatically with years of experience, and that the fix is to try harder rather than apply the right specific techniques. Against each, he argues classroom management is a learnable, specialized skill rather than an innate trait, that experience alone often produces stagnation or decline without deliberate adjustment, and that effort misapplied can actually cause teachers to lose ground. He closes urging readers to stop believing these myths and commit fully to the SCM approach rather than partially adopting it.
points: Classroom management challenges from before the pandemic are predicted to resume once in-person teaching fully returns.
Myth #1 is that some people are innately incapable of good classroom management, regardless of appearance, personality, or generation.
Myth #2 is that skill improves automatically with years of teaching experience; the piece argues it often plateaus or declines instead.
Myth #3 is that simply working harder improves classroom management, when the real requirement is applying specific, correct techniques.
The recommended fix is committing fully to the approach rather than partially adopting select pieces of it.
quotes: If you’re teaching online, then you know that classroom management is now a lot easier .
Because, if you were struggling with behavior before the pandemic, then you’ll struggle when it’s over. You see, classroom management doesn’t get better on its own.
But great classroom management isn’t just for the lucky few. You don’t have to look a certain way. You don’t have to talk a certain way or have a certain personality type.
Many teachers comfort themselves with the notion that the longer they teach, the better they’ll get. The opposite is true.
The idea that the harder you work, the better you’ll get at classroom management is baloney. It’s far more likely that you’ll spin your wheels or even lose ground.
Don’t dabble. Don’t pick and choose. Don’t overthink it. Just dive in and follow it like a paint by numbers Degas.
